risks.title: Geopolitical tensions and trade wars
risks.summary: Trade tensions, particularly with China and other Asian countries, threaten Apple's supply chain and could lead to cost increases or shortages.
risks.score_rationale: Risk is placed at the start of Macroeconomic and Industry Risks section, with strong language on uncertainty, potential escalation, and direct impact on supply chain and tariffs. Text mentions measures announced in Q2 2025 and sector inquiries (e.g., semiconductors), reinforcing timeliness and severity. Geopolitical category carries high weighting given Asian concentration. (default score, to be refined)

risks.title: Dependence on Asian supply chain
risks.summary: Apple relies heavily on external manufacturers in Asia, exposing the company to supply disruptions in case of local crisis or conflict.
risks.score_rationale: Document emphasizes that majority of manufacturing occurs in Asia (China, Vietnam, Taiwan, etc.) via outsourced partners. Geographic concentration is explicitly linked to major risks in case of disruption. Language stresses difficulty of rapid substitution, and risk is amplified by single sources. Central position in 10-K with high intensity. (default score, to be refined)

risks.title: Aggressive competition in technology markets
risks.summary: Apple faces intense competition from technology giants capable of selling at a loss, threatening its margins and market position.
risks.score_rationale: Risk is described as structural, with margin pressure, product imitation, and low pricing. Apple acknowledges minority market share in several key segments. Language is repetitive and emphasizes constant threat, though risk is stable versus prior year. Competition category carries medium to high weighting. (default score, to be refined)

risks.title: Disruptions from global economic conditions
risks.summary: Deterioration in global economic conditions could reduce demand for Apple's expensive products, affecting sales and profitability.
risks.score_rationale: Risk is broadly developed, with mention of recession, inflation, interest rates, and consumer confidence. Directly linked to demand for Apple products, often considered premium. Text cites impacts on customers, suppliers, and liquidity. Strong language and early position in document. High Macro weighting. (default score, to be refined)

risks.title: Cyberattacks and digital security risks
risks.summary: Apple is exposed to cyberattacks, notably ransomware, which could disrupt services and harm reputation.
risks.score_rationale: Risk is mentioned in context of business interruptions (e.g., ransomware). While less developed than others, it is associated with direct threats to services and infrastructure. Language is preventive but serious. Cybersecurity category is critical for technology company. Secondary but implicit position in multiple threats. (default score, to be refined)

risks.title: Dependence on single or limited suppliers
risks.summary: Apple uses many components from a single supplier, increasing disruption risk if this partner faces issues.
risks.score_rationale: Text explicitly mentions dependence on single sources for critical components. A single supplier problem can have major consequences, amplified by supply chain complexity. Strong language on potential impact ('exacerbate any negative consequences'). Existential risk in case of major failure. Industrial category highly weighted here. (default score, to be refined)

risks.title: Innovation and accelerated refresh cycles
risks.summary: Apple must constantly innovate to maintain competitiveness, but launch failures or delays could harm results and reputation.
risks.score_rationale: Risk is central in Business Risks section, with language insisting on constant innovation necessity. Launch failure or transition failure can strongly impact revenue. Text mentions technical, production, and market acceptance challenges. Though recurring, language intensity and competitive pressure justify high severity. (default score, to be refined)

ai_positioning.summary: No significant mention of artificial intelligence, machine learning, or related technologies was found in Apple's 10-K document for fiscal year 2025.
